methods.label: Perpendicular diagonals
methods.explanation:
Use the outward placement of the equilateral triangles shown in the diagram. Each apex lies on the perpendicular bisector of its base, which makes the diagonals of \(KLMN\) easier to find than its sides.

The square has side length \(4\), since its area is \(16\). An equilateral triangle of side \(4\) has an altitude that bisects its base. By the Pythagorean theorem, its altitude is
\[
h=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt3.
\]
Let \(O\) be the center of \(ABCD\). Its distance to each side is \(2\), so
\[
OK=OL=OM=ON=2+2\sqrt3.
\]
The points \(K,O,M\) lie on the perpendicular bisectors of the horizontal sides, while \(L,O,N\) lie on those of the vertical sides. Thus \(KM\) and \(LN\) are perpendicular and meet at \(O\).

Joining \(O\) to the four apices divides \(KLMN\) into four right triangles, each with perpendicular legs \(2+2\sqrt3\). Therefore its area is
\[
4\left(\frac12(2+2\sqrt3)^2\right)
=2(16+8\sqrt3)
=32+16\sqrt3.
\]
The answer is \(32+16\sqrt3\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses square midlines, equilateral-triangle altitudes, the Pythagorean theorem, and elementary triangle areas.

methods.label: Adding the pieces
methods.explanation:
With the outward placement shown, partition \(KLMN\) into the central square, the four given equilateral triangles, and the four corner triangles \(KBL,LCM,MDN,NAK\). We can find the area of each type separately.

The square has side \(4\). Each equilateral triangle has altitude
\[
\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt3,
\]
because its altitude bisects the base. Thus each has area \(\frac12\cdot4\cdot2\sqrt3=4\sqrt3\).

At \(B\), the square contributes a \(90^\circ\) angle and the two adjacent equilateral triangles contribute \(60^\circ\) each. The remaining angle is
\[
\angle KBL=360^\circ-90^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ=150^\circ.
\]
Also, \(BK=BL=4\). Extend \(KB\) beyond \(B\), and drop a perpendicular from \(L\) to this extended line. The resulting right triangle has hypotenuse \(BL=4\) and angle \(30^\circ\) at \(B\). Its leg opposite \(30^\circ\) is half its hypotenuse, so the height from \(L\) to line \(KB\) is \(2\). Consequently,
\[
\text{area of }KBL=\frac12\cdot4\cdot2=4.
\]
The other three corner triangles have the same side lengths and included angle, so each also has area \(4\).

The pieces have disjoint interiors and fill the outer quadrilateral. Its area is therefore
\[
16+4(4\sqrt3)+4(4)=32+16\sqrt3,
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: This independent area decomposition uses elementary angle subtraction and the 30-degree right-triangle property, with no trigonometry.
